stem: A nurse has an unresolved concern about a client's care and determines that formal escalation within the organization is needed. Which action is appropriate?

options.A: Document the concern but take no further action unless harm occurs
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift before deciding whether anyone else should be notified
options.C: Use the facility's chain of command and notify the next appropriate supervisory level
options.D: Ask an uninvolved coworker to decide whether the concern deserves further action

rationale: The 2026 NCSBN Test Plan identifies the chain of command as an advocacy resource and directs nurses to report identified client-care issues to appropriate personnel. Therefore, when a concern requires formal escalation, using the facility's chain of command is appropriate. A and B delay or stop needed escalation, and D transfers the decision to an uninvolved peer rather than using the formal escalation resource.
educational_objective: Use the organizational chain of command as an advocacy resource when a client-care concern requires escalation to appropriate personnel.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Appendix A, Management of Care, printed p.20 / PDF p.24, Advocacy: 'Use advocacy resources appropriately (e.g., social worker, chain of command, interpreter)'; printed p.22 / PDF p.26, Performance Improvement: 'Report identified client care issues to appropriate personnel'
source_claim_supported: The chain of command is an appropriate advocacy resource, and identified client-care issues should be reported to appropriate personnel.
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, Appendix A, printed pp.20 and 22 / PDF pp.24 and 26 — Advocacy and Performance Improvement
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — advocacy and escalation through chain of command
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported universal sequence that a nurse must first discuss every safety concern with a provider before escalation. Reframed the item around the directly supported NCSBN rule that chain of command is an advocacy resource and client-care issues are reported to appropriate personnel. Simplified distractors and adjusted difficulty from hard to moderate.
audit_findings: C directly uses the NCSBN-listed advocacy resource. A and B inappropriately stop or delay escalation; D substitutes an uninvolved peer for the formal escalation pathway. The corrected stem avoids assuming a universal first-contact sequence. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
